name: Jeriel
overview: Jeriel is a male figure from the tribe of Issachar, identified specifically as the son of Tola. His mention is brief and primarily genealogical, without additional narrative details or notes. This positions him within the lineage of Issachar as recorded in Scripture.
namesAndTitles: The name Jeriel means 'founded of God' or 'God will see,' reflecting a theophoric element referencing El, the God of Israel. This name highlights a connection to divine foundation or oversight, though it was not given directly by God according to the record.
familyAndRelationships: Jeriel is explicitly recorded as the son of Tola. Beyond this father-son relationship, Scripture does not provide further family connections or relationships for Jeriel.
scriptureSignificance: Jeriel's significance lies in his place within the genealogical records of the tribe of Issachar, serving to document the descendants of Tola. While he does not have a prominent narrative role, his inclusion preserves the continuity of God's covenant people and their tribal heritage.
